compiled_state.title: [LiteLLM integration]: Shipped to main without functional CI review -> 'litellm' dep missing in llm-review runner -> 0 specialists ever ran
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

The LiteLLM integration (epic 09b0-1d25 / story 298a + the `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` Python pipeline; see commits 29dfaff69a, 09846ae1a6, f3f6fa3053, 56ffe5bc52, 2f97c973bb) was implemented and merged to main, but the `litellm` Python dependency it depends on is not installed in the GitHub Actions environment that runs the `llm-review` job. Every specialist dispatch since the integration landed has crashed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'litellm'`. No deep-tier LLM review has ever produced real findings against any PR under the LiteLLM-based pipeline — including the PR(s) that introduced the LiteLLM integration itself.

This is a self-referential failure: the integration that IS the review pipeline was merged without the review pipeline functioning. The companion P0 (silent-pass exit code, fcea-6e83-ebad-49af) is what hid the regression for as long as it has been live.

## Expected Behavior

Any change to `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py`, `runner.py`, or any module importing `litellm` should:
1. Be reviewed by a real, executing LLM review run before merge to main
2. Have its CI environment validated to include `litellm` (and any other Python dependencies the integration requires) at install time
3. Have a smoke test that imports `litellm` at the top of the relevant runner and exits non-zero on import failure — wired as a required check before the LiteLLM-dependent review job runs

## Actual Behavior

- LiteLLM integration commits (29dfaff69a + earlier) merged to main
- The CI environment for the `llm-review` job does NOT install `litellm` (no `pip install litellm` step, no `requirements.txt` entry, or the install step is misconfigured)
- Every subsequent `llm-review` invocation: 3 specialists dispatched, 3 specialists crash on import, 3 `specialist_error` findings emitted, job exits 0 (PASS) due to bug fcea-6e83-ebad-49af
- Net effect: LiteLLM integration has been live on main with zero PRs ever receiving an actual deep-tier LLM review since its merge

## Evidence

- PR #52, llm-review job 74551374067 — 3 ModuleNotFoundError specialist_errors, exit 0 in 5s
- Run 25417143564 (HEAD `eb26cd7ef9` on `worktree-20260505-185224`)
- Likely earlier failures on every PR / CI run since the LiteLLM integration commits — this audit checked one PR; the assumption is the same failure has been ongoing since merge

## Affected Paths

- `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` — `import litellm`
- `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py` — same
- `.github/workflows/ci-llm-review.yml` (or equivalent) — missing `pip install litellm` (or missing `requirements*.txt` reference)
- `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` / `requirements-ci.txt` — likely doesn't include `litellm`

## Suggested Fix Direction

1. **Add `litellm` to CI install step**: identify the canonical CI dependency manifest for the llm-review job (`requirements-ci.txt`, `pyproject.toml [tool.dso.ci]`, or workflow inline `pip install`) and add `litellm` plus any transitive deps the integration uses (`fastapi`, etc. if applicable). Pin to a version verified to work.
2. **Smoke-import gate at job start**: before dispatching specialists, run `python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.__version__)"` and fail the job non-zero if it errors. Logs the version into the job summary for traceability.
3. **Backfill ALL prior PRs that were "reviewed" under this regime**: query GitHub for PRs merged to main since the LiteLLM integration commit; flag any whose llm-review check passed in <30 seconds (proxy for silent-no-op) for re-review. This may surface real findings that were hidden by the regression.
4. **Add a regression test**: a CI test that builds the runner image without `litellm`, dispatches it, and asserts the smoke-import gate fails the job. Lock in the behavior so a future requirements drift is caught immediately.
5. **Pair with fcea-6e83-ebad-49af**: that bug fixes the silent-pass exit-code; this one fixes the underlying dependency miss. Both must land together — neither alone restores the review tier.

## Priority Justification (P0)

P0 because:
- Every PR merged under this regime since the LiteLLM integration is unreviewed by the deep tier despite reporting green
- The integration that implements the review pipeline shipped untested by the review pipeline — the gap could only be observed by reading job logs, not check status
- Cumulative correctness debt grows with every additional merge until fixed (every newly-merged PR also missed deep review)
- Required CI check (`llm-review`) is reporting non-information

This combined with fcea-6e83-ebad-49af is a complete-system-failure of the deep-tier review gate. Both are P0; both must be fixed in the same change-set.

## Related Tickets

- fcea-6e83-ebad-49af (P0, this turn) — companion: silent-pass exit code that hid the regression
- f420-2607-1e29-4b04 (closed) — cited_lines fix that depended on this pipeline working
- 09b0-1d25-1a7d-4cf1 (epic, closed) — PR Merge Remediation Loop, which assumed the review pipeline functioned
- 62ae-26ec-1a99-4014 (closed) — brainstorm GitHub-capability probe; this incident is similarly an "external dependency that was assumed but never validated" failure mode

## Process Lesson

Filing this also serves as a forcing function for /dso:brainstorm to add a "ship integration with its own functional CI gate" check to the External Dependencies probe — analogous to the GitHub auto-merge probe added in cef107b8cc (2026-05-05). A LiteLLM integration's "external dependency" is its own runtime environment.

comments.body: Classification: compound bug cluster — 3 related P0 bugs in CI llm-review pipeline. Routing to cluster investigation. Sub-issues: (1) d99c-f4d4 litellm ModuleNotFoundError runtime failure, (2) fcea-6e83 exit-0 silent pass on all-specialist failure, (3) b38d-1781 pre-merge validation gap. All relate to same llm-review CI subsystem.

comments.body: Fixed: (1) litellm dep installed in CI via added pip install step — prevents ModuleNotFoundError; (2) exit-1 added to runner.py when all specialists fail — prevents silent pass; (3) structural test test_llm_review_installs_litellm enforces dep installation in template; (4) step-count regression guard updated from 2→3 steps. Code at 6a6a3643beae0472f70d09122927546889312264.
